findings.title: condition tied to replacement
findings.claim: The response connector binds the defection condition to divine replacement.
findings.mechanism: The result-marking connector at the supplied response morpheme links the conditional protasis to its answer, so withdrawal is met within the ayah by the stated divine response.
findings.reader_payoff: Withdrawal is heard as a condition with a stated answer rather than as the end of communal possibility.
findings.containment: This is a local connective relation; it does not assert how quickly the response unfolds.

findings.mechanism: The future particle delays the replacement relative to the defection clause without weakening its grammatical presentation as a promised response under divine control.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives both temporal unfolding and the steadiness of the promise.
findings.containment: A future horizon is marked; no calendar, duration, or sequence beyond the supplied clause is claimed.
